items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: Nice, John Mo. That's when he was only thing about him. He liked trombone correct and everything. But he wouldn't play with a fellow if he didn't play, you know, right.

ctx.x: What was the name of it? Once, I remember, even in the Defender. Wife, remember what? Had a wife and she played piano in Oregon, too. They had a job in some theater going around the country. And for a while were in West Virginia once, playing in the theater.

Yeah, he was very, very good. Nice, John Mo. That's when he was only thing about him. He liked trombone correct and everything. But he wouldn't play with a fellow if he didn't play, you know, right. You know, a man come in and played with him, played double with him, and get to blast him.
Maybe that's why some people thought he was sort of mean. Yeah. Some children come in, right.
